entry.title: Decide your worth!
entry.content:
Decide your worth!

Ones(your) worth is not something that can be measured by numbers, titles, or external validation. It is an intrinsic truth, deeply rooted within you….something only you can fully recognize and understand. While the world may try to define you through metrics, comparisons, or material achievements, the essence of value goes far beyond such superficial measures. You alone have the power to perceive and honor your worth beyond any societal constructs. But how do you truly judge your value? This is a deeply personal journey, one that no one else can undertake for you. When reflect on this, you will notice how many people go through life unaware of the impact their words or actions on others. They might think they’re being funny when making cutting remarks, completely oblivious to the harm or disrespect they may cause. Their lack of self-awareness blinds them to the weight of their intentions. In contrast, when you hold yourself in high regard . when we truly understand and respect our own values in that case we become acutely aware of your actions and words. When we strive to approach life with mindfulness, knowing that every sentence we spoke and every choice we made carries significance. Does this mean we are immune to mistakes? Not at all. Even when you value yourself deeply, you will still stumble and err. The difference lies in how you respond: if you acknowledge your missteps, reflect on them with honesty, and take responsibility for your actions. This self-awareness and accountability are what elevate your character and reinforce sense of worth.

True value is not about perfection; it’s about presence, integrity, and the courage to grow through every experience….good or bad. It’s about being fully conscious of who you are and strive to align your actions with your highest self. Only you can define what that means for you, and only you can live it authentically.

Decide your worth by yourself. Channelize, Analyze and Acknowledge.

KIKI

entry.title: Smell of Rajasthan
entry.content:
In the hazy realm between sleep and wakefulness, the familiar symphony of an Indian kitchen gently pulls me from my dreams. It’s a winter weekend morning and the aroma of something special. The heavenly smell of bajre ki roti with ghee wafts through the house.

Time moves differently in those moments, stretching and contracting like a cat in a sunbeam. As noon approaches, the world outside seems to slow down, caught in the drowsy heat of the afternoon. But then, cutting through the sleepy silence, comes the tinkling of a bell. It’s the ice cream seller, and suddenly I used to run despite the oppressive heat. Holding in my hand, a bowl of wheat. A barter that feels both ancient and timeless. The artificial orange flavor in a uniquely nostalgic combination, hiding spot among the mustard seed sacks from the winter harvest. It’s was the secret place.

In this moment, past and present blur together, and I still wonder if in parallel universe, my childhood self is waiting for the ice cream seller to ring the bell once more time before i again step into fast pace life.

KIKI

entry.title: Fear of living an average life

link.title: Fear of living an average life

entry.content:
Fear of Living an Average Life

Every morning, I wake up to the same routine: the alarm blares, I grab an Americano from the café, and sit in front of a screen. The world inside my phone buzzes with life story after story. As I scroll, a gnawing fear grips my heart: the fear of living an average life.

I watched people chasing their dreams while feeling tethered to mediocrity. Every day became a constant reminder of unfulfilled potential. Eventually, it led to mental exhaustion and a body that felt perpetually tired. This daily battle within myself finally forced me to pause my mundane routine. In that pause came an epiphany, one that made me reevaluate the direction of my life. A journey of self-discovery began, with a vow to transform my once-average life into something I would truly cherish. The adventure had begun.

When I look back, I see someone who was possibly living one of the best lives anyone could imagine and yet, here I am, someone who actually lived it. I grew up with perfect mental peace, full of confidence, flying without wings, unafraid of failure, with the freedom to do whatever I wanted, even in a South Asian household. I was surrounded by books of every kind, which later became the foundation of my deepest understanding of human behavior.

And yet, at the age of twenty-five, I found myself trapped in mental torment. I was calculating every moment, every feeling, every circumstance, all of which pushed me toward a terrible fear, a phobia of mundaneness. After enough reflection, the realization struck me: it was all coming from comparison.

I was comparing my worth and competence with everyone around me. I was only taking my first steps while everyone else seemed to be nearing the finish line. It was an unfair comparison, one that was deeply unkind to my soul.

How did I even learn to compare myself with others? Nobody taught me this at home, nor did I learn it in school. I learned it from a world of competition, where everyone was running toward… what? Maybe stability? Recognition?

And I guess I cannot calm my brain until I fully understand what and why’s. So I guess I will explore until then.

And yes! the journey begins.

A journey of self-reclamation. A journey to rediscover and hold on to the inner peace I always had. A journey toward struggles that I will claim as entirely my own.

This autumn brought me back to myself. ❤
